timed_text.text: Day 25
What happens in the five seconds after a mistake determines more about your performance than the mistake itself
Here's the pattern
Athlete makes error
Brain fires immediately
Replays the mistake
Catastrophises
The consequences
Athlete carries that weight into the next play
Next play breaks down spiral
The mistake didn't cost them the five seconds after did
Your job in those five seconds is one thing
Interruption you are not processing the mistake. You are not evaluating what went wrong. You have one job get back to the next play
Three steps
Reset word say it physical cue
Run it focus anchor return to it five seconds back in the game
Today you're drilling that sequence three times back to back until it's locked
On your screen you're going to walk through it right now

cards.prompt: A mistake just happened. 5 seconds. Step 1 — your reset word. Say it now.
Step 2 — your physical cue. Run it right now.
Step 3 — your focus anchor. Return to it. You're here. Next play.
Again. Mistake. Reset word. Physical cue. Focus anchor.
One more time. All three steps. Locked.
Describe what running that sequence felt like. Did it interrupt the spiral? What was hardest to execute?

timed_text.text: Drill that protocol and practice this week.
Make an intentional error and run it.
Make it automatic before competition demands it.
After you finish, day 25 is complete.
